transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Cole (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Solutions), Markus Lin (HelioScale CTO), Janelle Brooks (ML Eng), Ravi Singh (Platform), Sofia Park (Data Privacy)

[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ethan from Redwood, and this is Priya, our SE. We're gonna run through a parity deep-dive for migrating your inference from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to the Redwood API. quick introductions?
[00:14] Markus: Markus here — CTO at HelioScale. We're trying to consolidate multiple endpoints and drop our per-token variability. main concerns are latency consistency and data residency for EU customers.
[00:30] Janelle: Hi, Janelle. I own the ML infra and pipelines — mostly curious about runtime differences, KV cache behavior and how easy it is to port prompt engineering.
[00:43] Priya: great. We'll show an API mapping, console walk-though and Optimize recommendations. we'll call out any breaking parts for Together style responses too.
[00:58] Ravi: also, on the platform side, we need SSO + audit logs for compliance. and KMS integration because we rotate keys via our vault.
[01:10] Priya: noted. Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations and detailed audit logs; we'll show the console logging and role-based access shortly.
[01:20] Liam: quick note, we commonly see customers reference the 'KV cache' — sometimes transcribed as K V cache — we mean the prefix/KV caching in the runtime that preserves key/value for long conversations.

[02:05] Priya: OK, API parity. First slide (shared): request/response model. OpenAI-style call typically: model, prompt/messages, temperature, max_tokens. Anthropic/Together sometimes use different param names for top_p and response_format. Redwood's API is intentionally normalized — we accept messages (chat) and text completion, plus streaming and function/tool-calling.
[02:35] [screen share] Priya: here's an example mapping:
- OpenAI: messages -> Redwood: messages (same)
- Anthropic: prompt -> Redwood: messages with system role
- Together: sometimes returns different nested json for safety metadata — Redwood flattens safety metadata to headers and provides a side-channel.

[03:02] Janelle: will our existing Together client adapters break? we currently parse nested meta for tool hints.
[03:10] Priya: you might need a small adapter layer to map the together meta into Redwood's tool-calling format. usually 40–120 lines of transform. common gotcha is token counting differences — Redwood exposes token usage per response and per-route tokenization so you can calibrate.
[03:28] Markus: token counting — is it same as tiktoken? we use tiktoken v1 for billing alignment.
[03:35] Priya: Redwood uses an industry-aligned tokenizer that matches tiktoken in most common models; for some community model families we include a compatibility shim. We'll include a token mapping table in the parity sheet.

[05:00] Ethan: let's demo the console. I'll hand to Priya to flip to the model catalog and routing page.
[05:10] Priya: sure. (screen) Model catalog shows Redwood-verified profiles: latency/throughput for each variant. you can pin a model version and configure rollouts — canary, A/B, auto-fallback. here's a routing policy example: prefer low-latency region, fallback to cheaper variant if latency SLO violated.
[05:42] Ravi: does routing support tenant-scoped policies? we do per-customer SLA enforcement.
[05:48] Priya: yes, policies can be scoped by token, by project, or by API key so you can isolate per-tenant behavior.

[06:30] Priya: next, caching. Redwood's prefix and KV cache reduces repeated token compute. for multi-turn chat we often see 20–60% cost reduction in workloads with repetitive context. caveat: if you have PII that cannot be cached, there's an opt-out at route level.
[06:55] Sofia: that's important. we need to ensure cached data never stores PHI/PPI.
[07:02] Priya: completely — route-level cache controls and encryption at rest with customer-managed keys.

[07:45] [10:00] Priya: moving to Optimize. We recommend three levers: batching, quantization, and model family selection. For example, for high-throughput stateless generation we suggest dynamic batching with latency SLOs; for lower-latency chat we suggest small batch sizes and KV caching.
[08:12] Janelle: how does batching affect per-request latency jitter?
[08:17] Priya: good question — Redwood's continuous batching tries to fill micro-batches within a micro-sla window (e.g., 5–20ms) so typical added latency is minimal; but in very low QPS cases batching gives less benefit. Optimize provides workload-specific recommendations based on your token distribution.

[09:00] [09:30] Priya: quantization profiles — we support multiple quantization levels with measured quality regressions per model. We'll give you an example: int8 vs int4 tradeoffs on throughput and measured ROUGE/EM on your eval set. we can surface regression alerts tied to eval prompt-sets.
[09:45] Markus: can we run a quick benchmark with our golden prompts?
[09:50] Ethan: yes, that's a standard next step — share your prompts and we'll run a parity bench across the three vendors and Redwood.

[10:20] Janelle: curious about streaming and function/tool-calls — our current Together endpoints do stream but with a different chunk format.
[10:30] Priya: Redwood's streaming is chunked with standard SSE and supports function calling via structured JSON. the console shows sample function schemas and how to map Together style tool hints into Redwood's tool calling.

[11:10] [11:30] Priya: Security deep-dive — Redwood Private (VPC) and Dedicated options. For regulated workloads we offer private control plane with optional on-prem package. you mentioned EU residency?
[11:45] Markus: yes, we need data segregation for EU customers and an audit trail for GDPR.
[11:50] Priya: we can pin model serving to EU regions and enable customer-managed keys (KMS). audit logs show token-level activity and model version; we also support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for RBAC.
[12:12] Sofia: any gotchas with our existing vault rotation? we rotate keys hourly sometimes for edge cases.
[12:20] Priya: Redwood integrates with common KMS flows; for extreme rotation cadences we recommend Dedicated with HSM backing. we'll include the KMS integration notes.

[13:00] Ethan: let's talk about Dedicated sizing — Liam, you wanted to show cost profiles?
[13:08] Liam: yep. (screen) here's a sample Dedicated cluster for a 100 qps 1k-token median workload. we show GPU counts, expected throughput, and sample cost per 1M tokens. apples-to-apples: with batching and KV cache on Redwood we often see 30–50% lower unit cost vs naive single-request endpoints.
[13:42] Markus: curious about burst handling. our traffic spikes irregularly.
[13:48] Liam: Dedicated supports reserved baseline + burst credits to hosted capacity; policy-based autoscaling can be tuned with warm-up windows.

[14:20] [15:00] Janelle: are there code samples for porting clients? we have a mono-repo with adapters to OpenAI and Together, want something minimal.
[14:30] Priya: yes, we'll provide adapter snippets. typical pattern: small shim to translate request params, a tokenizer harmonizer to align counts, and an optional response normalizer if you're extracting tool-call payloads.

[15:05] Ravi: latency numbers — do you have p50/p95 for typical chat workloads?
[15:10] Priya: for a 8k context model on A100-ish hardware we see p50 ~ 35–60ms per token in optimized paths; p95 can be 2–3x depending on sequence length. our catalog has measured profiles per model.
[15:35] Markus: those per-token numbers seem optimistic compared to our current prod — are they measured on similar batch patterns?
[15:42] Priya: yes, measurements reflect continuous batching and kernel selection; we'll attach raw benchmark scripts so you can reproduce.

[16:10] [17:00] Priya: demo: I'll run a live parity conversion for one of your Together endpoints. I'm pasting a sample Together response and converting to Redwood call live.
[16:20] [screen shows code] Priya: here — Together call has nested safety metadata and tool hints. I'll transform nested metadata into Redwood headers, pass messages as chat array, and wire tool-call schema to the functions param.
[17:12] Janelle: looks straightforward. are there any edge cases for streaming cancellation? we rely on being able to cancel mid-stream.
[17:20] Priya: Redwood streaming supports client-side cancellation tokens. cancellation semantics may differ slightly (we flush partial tokens), we'll document.

[18:00] [19:00] Ethan: moving to parity sheet — Priya, walk through the row examples.
[18:12] Priya: row one: 'Auth' — Together uses API key header X-Together-Key, OpenAI uses Authorization Bearer, Redwood accepts Bearer or API-Key header and also supports mTLS for private deployments. Row two: 'Tool schema' — Together nested -> Redwood functions JSON. Row three: 'Token counting' — small diffs, we recommend running token sample set.
[18:45] Markus: any mapping for safety labels? we currently surface safety scores to our moderation pipeline.
[18:52] Priya: we expose safety metadata via response headers and a sidecar payload; you can keep your moderation pipeline with minimal changes.

[20:00] [22:00] Priya: now Optimize recommendations specific to HelioScale. Based on the usage pattern you shared: median prompt length ~ 400 tokens, high re-use of boilerplate instructions, we recommend: 1) enable prefix cache on routes with sensitive transformations disabled, 2) int8 quantization for baseline evaluation, int4 for cost test, 3) route-level policy that routes EU customers to EU-only cluster.
[22:40] Janelle: can Optimize auto-suggest these settings?
[22:45] Priya: yes, there's an Optimize recommendation engine that runs on a sample trace and suggests batch sizes and quantization levels with estimated cost delta. we can run it on your sample traffic.

[24:00] [25:00] Ravi: about evaluating quality regressions with quantization — what tooling do you provide?
[25:08] Priya: we have an eval harness — you provide golden prompts and expected outputs, and we compute BLEU/ROUGE/F1 and also a human review queue for edge-cases. alerts can be tied to a Slack channel or to the console.

[26:30] [27:00] Priya: time for Q&A — Markus?
[27:10] Markus: two quick items: 1) contract terms — we need a 99.9% SLA and data deletion on deprovision models, 2) legal wants more info on subprocessors and audit logs.
[27:28] Ethan: SLA is available for Dedicated and Private; hosted has standard terms we can upgrade. we'll send the data deletion playbook and subprocessors list.
[27:42] Sofia: do you support exportable audit logs for our SIEM?
[27:48] Priya: yes, logs can stream to your SIEM via secure pipeline; we support S3 export and direct syslog, plus structured JSON events for each API call.

[29:00] [31:00] Janelle: small UX question: how do rollouts look in the console for A/B? we want to route 10% traffic to a new model for quality testing.
[31:12] Priya: (shares) you can set rollout rules: percent-based split, canary by user-id, or cookie. telemetry surfaces p50/p95 and quality deltas for the groups. you can set auto-fallback if error rate exceeds threshold.

[32:00] [33:00] Ethan: let's capture explicit next steps and owners real quick.
[32:10] Markus: we'll send prompt sets and sample traffic metrics; follow up with a POC if costs look acceptable.
[32:22] Janelle: also want the adapter example and token count harmonizer.
[32:30] Ethan: Priya will share parity mapping sheet + adapter snippets. I'll send pricing and Dedicated sizing. We'll plan a POC kickoff once HelioScale shares prompts and we validate bench results.

[33:45] [34:00] Priya: ok, rapid fire technical notes / gotchas:
- Together nested tool hints -> Redwood functions mapping required
- Token-counting alignment (tune tokenizer shim)
- Streaming chunk formats differ; cancellation semantics slightly different
- Cache opt-out for PII routes

[35:30] [38:00] Markus: any documented case studies for consolidation from multiple vendors?
[35:40] Ethan: yes, we'll include case studies (anonymized) where customers consolidated and reduced ops surface.

[38:45] Janelle: can we run the bench on-prem vs hosted comparisons? our compliance team prefers on-prem for some EU workloads.
[38:52] Priya: definitely. we can spin a Private deployment benchmark — it takes some coordination, but we have a checklist.

[40:00] [41:00] Priya: one more deep-dive: failure modes and graceful degradation. Redwood supports auto-fallback to cheaper variants or smaller context models. you can configure per-route fallback policies and circuit-breakers.
[41:20] Ravi: good — we need deterministic fallbacks during regulatory incidents.

[43:00] [44:00] Ethan: time check — about 12 minutes left. any final tech asks?
[44:10] Janelle: can the Optimize recommendations be run continuously during POC to auto-tune batch sizes?
[44:18] Priya: for POC we run offline Optimize and recommend, but we also offer a 'suggest-only' mode in early phases. auto-tune can be enabled in mature deployments.

[45:00] [47:00] Markus: I'm concerned about subtle output diffs when switching models — our legal reviews a few categories of responsivity. can Redwood help with regression testing?
[45:10] Priya: yes — regression alerts tied to your golden prompt set. we can run diff reports and flag drops in key metrics. human-in-the-loop review is built in.

[48:00] Ethan: ok wrapping up — let's restate next steps.
[48:10] Priya: action items: I'll send the parity mapping sheet and adapter code, plus token mapping and tokenizer shim.
[48:20] Ethan: I'll send pricing and Dedicated sizing and propose POC timeline.
[48:25] Markus: we'll share prompts and traffic profile by next Tue.

[49:00] [50:00] Sofia: one last compliance ask: please include your subprocessor list and SOC 2 cert path.
[50:10] Ethan: will do.

[50:30] [51:00] Priya: TL;DR: porting is straightforward with a thin adapter. main work: token alignment, tool-call mapping, and planned bench to validate quality. Optimize can give a clear cost/latency tradeoff and Dedicated gives predictable throughput for spikes.

[52:00] Markus: thanks, appreciated — this gives us a clear path forward.
[52:12] Ethan: great. we'll follow up with the sheets and schedule a POC kickoff if you approve. thanks everyone.
[52:25] Janelle: thanks all.
[52:28] Ravi: thanks.
[52:30] Meeting end.
